% docs/deliverable/preamble.tex
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
% THE EXECUTION OF docs/deliverable/RECIPE.md. Every block carries the recipe step it
% implements. RECIPE.md is the source of truth and this file is not free to disagree with
% it: `scripts/wt173_typography_probe.py --verify` holds the recipe to a fresh build, and
% `docs/deliverable/verify-layout.sh` holds THIS document's page count and per-page text
% hash. Do not edit a value here -- edit the recipe, re-measure, then bring this file to it.
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

% ---- RECIPE step 3 · document class ---------------------------------------------------
\documentclass[11pt,letterpaper]{article}

% ---- RECIPE step 6 · fonts BY PATH, never by family name ------------------------------
% A Path= load either finds that exact file or errors out. A family-NAME load asks the
% operating system, which is helpful, which is the problem (preflight.sh, header).
\usepackage{fontspec}
\usepackage{unicode-math}
\setmainfont{LibertinusSerif-Regular.otf}[
  Path            = ./fonts/ ,
  ItalicFont      = LibertinusSerif-Italic.otf ,
  BoldFont        = LibertinusSerif-Bold.otf ,
  BoldItalicFont  = LibertinusSerif-BoldItalic.otf ]
\setsansfont{LibertinusSans-Regular.otf}[
  Path            = ./fonts/ ,
  ItalicFont      = LibertinusSans-Italic.otf ,
  BoldFont        = LibertinusSans-Bold.otf ]
\setmonofont{Inconsolatazi4-Regular.otf}[
  Path            = ./fonts/ ,
  BoldFont        = Inconsolatazi4-Bold.otf ,
  Scale           = MatchLowercase ]
\setmathfont{LibertinusMath-Regular.otf}[ Path = ./fonts/ ]

% Display cut of the serif -- the title scale of step 11, and nothing else.
\newfontfamily\wtdisplayfont{LibertinusSerifDisplay-Regular.otf}[ Path = ./fonts/ ]

% ---- wt175 · THE FOUR MARKS NO LIBERTINUS FACE CARRIES --------------------------------
% MEASURED at wealthTensor-94, not assumed: the corpus uses 75 distinct non-ASCII
% characters and SIX are absent from LibertinusSerif-Regular. Two are mathematics and are
% set in math mode out of LibertinusMath, which has them (U+2299 CIRCLED DOT OPERATOR,
% U+1D4A9 SCRIPT CAPITAL N). The other four --
%     U+2713 CHECK MARK      95x        U+29D7 BLACK HOURGLASS   17x
%     U+270E LOWER RIGHT PENCIL 13x     U+26A0 WARNING SIGN       1x
% -- are carried by NONE of the fifteen fonts this deliverable had vendored, and they are
% not decoration: they are the citation-verification notation the References sections
% DEFINE in their own prose (paper-I lines 593-595). LaTeX reports an absent glyph as
% "Missing character:" in the log and then sets NOTHING, so all 126 marks would have
% disappeared out of a build that exited 0. That is the overfull-box disease in a second
% organ, and build.sh now fails the build on both.
%
% The repair KEEPS ADR-002's discipline rather than re-opening it: FreeSerif.otf is
% vendored into ./fonts/ and checksummed in FONTS.tsv exactly like the other fifteen, and
% loaded by Path. Nothing here asks the operating system for a font.
% Declared with ONE cut in every shape on purpose: the four marks are symbols, they have
% no bold or italic design, and a mark inside a bold heading would otherwise raise
% "Font shape undefined" and fall back silently. Saying it explicitly costs nothing and
% vendors three fewer megabytes than shipping the Bold and Italic cuts to be ignored.
\newfontfamily\wtmarksfont{FreeSerif.otf}[ Path = ./fonts/ ,
  BoldFont = FreeSerif.otf , ItalicFont = FreeSerif.otf , BoldItalicFont = FreeSerif.otf ]
\newcommand{\wtmark}[1]{{\wtmarksfont #1}}

% ---- RECIPE step 8 · page geometry ----------------------------------------------------
% US Letter 614.295pt x 794.97pt. Left and right margins 162.6075pt, top 72.27pt; the
% bottom comes out at 92.7pt and exceeds the top ON PURPOSE -- the block is optically
% centred rather than geometrically centred.
\usepackage[letterpaper,
  textwidth=289.08pt, textheight=630.0pt,
  left=162.6075pt, top=72.27pt, heightrounded=false]{geometry}

% ---- RECIPE steps 4, 5, 9, 12 · body size, leading, grid, display maths ---------------
% 11.0pt on 14.0pt, set EXPLICITLY rather than inherited, so the leading is not the class's
% guess (step 4's own words). textheight 630.0pt is exactly 45 leadings, so the block
% closes flush on the baseline grid. The display skips of step 12 are declared HERE, inside
% \normalsize, because that is where LaTeX resets them -- setting them once at the top level
% would be silently undone by the first \small in a table.
\makeatletter
\renewcommand\normalsize{%
  \@setfontsize\normalsize{11.0}{14.0}%
  \abovedisplayskip      11.0pt \@plus 3.0pt \@minus 6.0pt
  \abovedisplayshortskip \z@    \@plus 3.0pt
  \belowdisplayshortskip 6.5pt  \@plus 3.5pt \@minus 3.0pt
  \belowdisplayskip      11.0pt \@plus 3.0pt \@minus 6.0pt
  \let\@listi\@listI}
\makeatother
\normalsize
\setlength{\parindent}{17.0pt}
\setlength{\parskip}{0.0pt plus 1.0pt}

% ---- RECIPE step 10 · microtype, loaded AFTER the fonts -------------------------------
% This is what makes the measured characters-per-line of step 7 reproducible. Without it
% the paragraphs break differently and the layout hashes do not reproduce.
\usepackage{microtype}

% ---- RECIPE step 13 · inline code identifiers -----------------------------------------
% At this measure an inline monospace run fits 55 characters; the corpus's longest
% identifier is 64. \url breaks it at its underscores and INSERTS NO CHARACTER, so what a
% reader copies out of the PDF is still what runs. Not solved by centring (measured: still
% 41.36pt too wide) and not by shrinking the code font, which defeats why ADR-002 chose
% this cut. wt175_md2tex.lua is what routes identifiers here instead of to \texttt.
\usepackage{url}
\urlstyle{tt}
\def\UrlBreaks{\do\_}
% AMENDED AT wealthTensor-94, FROM THE REAL BUILD, AND RECIPE.md step 13 CARRIES THE SAME
% AMENDMENT. `\do\_` alone was written for IDENTIFIERS and the corpus's code spans are not
% all identifiers: measured on the four manuscripts, the spans also contain repository URLs
% (`https://github.com/jasoncbraatz/wealth-tensor`, 47 characters, no underscore anywhere)
% and bare 64-character git SHAs (no break opportunity of any kind). Those overflowed the
% measure by 30.8pt and 62.8pt respectively. xurl adds break opportunities without INSERTING
% A CHARACTER, which is the property step 13 actually asks for -- what a reader copies out of
% the PDF still runs -- so it satisfies the step's stated reason rather than only its letter.
% It is also the package pandoc's own generated preamble reaches for, for this exact reason.
\usepackage{xurl}
% AMENDED AT wealthTensor-109b, FROM THE RENDERED PAGE, and RECIPE.md step 13 carries the same
% amendment. xurl fixed the two overflows -94 measured and, in doing so, silently discarded the
% underscore-only rule this step was written around: it grants a break opportunity at EVERY
% character, so `wt083_tier_ladder_antialignment` was set as `wt083_ti` / `er_ladder_anti...`.
% Measured on the built capture against the four manuscripts as ground truth: sixteen MID-WORD
% breaks against ten at underscores. Step 13's stated reason survived that change -- nothing is
% inserted, so what a reader copies still runs -- and its READABILITY did not, which is why the
% defect sat through every pass that read step 13 rather than the page.
%
% The repair is not to drop xurl: the 47-character repository URL and the 64-character SHA have
% no underscore between them and genuinely need breaks anywhere. It is that the two populations
% were never the same population. \url keeps xurl's behaviour and carries URLs and SHAs;
% \wtident carries snake_case identifiers and breaks ONLY at underscores, which is where a
% reader's eye expects the seam. \DeclareUrlCommand scopes \UrlBreaks to the command, so this
% cannot leak back into \url. wt175_md2tex.lua decides which span gets which.
% THE SEAM SET, widened once at authoring time after measuring the first attempt. Restricting
% \wtident to `\do\_` alone fixed 9 of the 16 mid-word breaks and left 7, all of them an
% identifier living INSIDE a path -- `scripts/wt083_tier_ladder_antialignment.py` is not
% `^[%w_]+$`, so it fell through to \url and was cut at `wt083_ti`. A path has seams too; they
% are just spelt `/` and `.` rather than `_`. So the command breaks at every seam a reader
% recognises, and only a token with NO seam at all -- a bare 64-character SHA -- still needs
% xurl's break-anywhere rule, which is exactly the case -94 added it for.
\DeclareUrlCommand\wtident{\urlstyle{tt}\def\UrlBreaks{\do\_\do\/\do\.\do\-\do\:}}

% ---- figures ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
% wealthTensor-110. The corpus carried ZERO figures until now, and this preamble did not even
% load graphicx -- FIGURES.tsv says so in its own header, and P13f's @zero-figures sentinel is
% the claim that made that absence checkable rather than merely true. The v2 review pair is
% the first document here with pictures in it, so the ability to set one arrives here.
%
% NOT A FLOAT, deliberately. Every figure in these manuscripts is followed IMMEDIATELY by a
% blockquote that reads "Figure N -- ..." and IS the caption. A LaTeX float would carry the
% picture to the top of some later page and leave its caption behind, pointing at nothing --
% the orphan defect this corpus already has a name for. So the picture sets exactly where the
% author put it, and the caption stays under it by construction rather than by hope.
\usepackage{graphicx}
% THE FIGURES GET THEIR OWN MEASURE, exactly as the wide tables do, and for the same reason.
% The body measure is 289.08pt inside 162.6pt margins -- a narrow scholarly block. The nine
% charts are drawn 540bp wide, so setting them to the body measure scales them to 0.53 and
% takes their axis labels down to about six points: legible under a loupe, not on paper. The
% first cut did exactly that and the proof page showed it.
%
% 460pt leaves 77pt of paper on each side (the ink check demands 18bp, so this clears it four
% times over) and lands the charts at 0.85 -- large enough to read, still visibly a figure set
% into a narrow column rather than a poster.
\newlength{\wtfigmeasure}\setlength{\wtfigmeasure}{460.0pt}
% NOT A FLOAT, deliberately. Every figure here is followed IMMEDIATELY by a blockquote that
% reads "Figure N -- ..." and IS the caption. A LaTeX float would carry the picture to the top
% of some later page and leave its caption behind pointing at nothing -- the orphan defect this
% corpus already has a name for. So the picture sets where the author put it, and the caption
% stays under it by construction rather than by hope.
%
% The width is CLAMPED rather than trusted: anything wider than the figure measure would be an
% overfull box, which build.sh promotes to fatal.
\newcommand{\wtfig}[1]{%
  \par\addvspace{11.0pt}%
  \setbox0=\hbox{\includegraphics{#1}}%
  \ifdim\wd0>\wtfigmeasure
    \setbox0=\hbox{\includegraphics[width=\wtfigmeasure]{#1}}%
  \fi
  % \hss on BOTH sides, and that is the whole trick. A box wider than the measure, set with
  % \hspace* and \makebox, is an OVERFULL BOX by exactly its overhang -- and build.sh promotes
  % an overfull box to fatal, so the first cut of this command refused its own build nine
  % times over, once per figure. \hss shrinks infinitely, so the enclosing box meets \hsize
  % honestly while the picture hangs equally into both margins.
  \hbox to\hsize{\hss\box0\hss}%
  \par\addvspace{2.0pt}}

% ---- RECIPE step 14 · tables ----------------------------------------------------------
% booktabs only: \toprule, \midrule, \bottomrule. No vertical rules and no \hline.
\usepackage{booktabs}
\usepackage{longtable}
\usepackage{array}
\usepackage{calc}
\setlength{\floatsep}{12.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 2.0pt}
\setlength{\textfloatsep}{20.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 4.0pt}
\setlength{\intextsep}{12.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 2.0pt}
\setlength{\abovecaptionskip}{10.0pt}
\setlength{\belowcaptionskip}{0.0pt}

% ---- what pandoc's LaTeX writer assumes its template provides -----------------------
% This preamble replaces pandoc's default template, so the handful of macros that template
% defines have to be defined here or the build dies on an undefined control sequence.
% \real comes from calc, loaded above, and is what pandoc's longtable column widths use.
\providecommand{\tightlist}{\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}}
\providecommand{\texorpdfstring}[2]{#1}
% Pandoc wraps every UNCAPTIONED longtable in `{\def\LTcaptype{none} ... }` and its own
% generated preamble answers that with a DUMMY COUNTER, not with the caption package:
% `\newcounter{none} % for unnumbered tables`. Without it, longtable's machinery reaches
% \refstepcounter{none} and the build dies with "No counter 'none' defined" -- on all
% thirty tables. Taken verbatim from `pandoc -s -t latex` on a one-row table, which is the
% only authority on what pandoc's output needs.
\newcounter{none}
\usepackage{etoolbox}
\makeatletter
\patchcmd\longtable{\par}{\if@noskipsec\mbox{}\fi\par}{}{}
\makeatother
% four footnotes in the corpus; this is pandoc's own provision for footnotes in a longtable
\IfFileExists{footnotehyper.sty}{\usepackage{footnotehyper}}{\usepackage{footnote}}
\makesavenoteenv{longtable}

% ---- line breaking at a 289.08pt measure ----------------------------------------------
% A four-inch measure is narrow, and a short paragraph of long unbreakable tokens (an author
% block: "Jason C. Braatz Independent researcher jason@braatzresearch.com") can leave TeX no
% break it will accept, at which point it sets an OVERFULL line -- text physically outside
% the measure. \emergencystretch gives the line breaker a third pass with extra
% stretchability, so it produces a LOOSE line instead of a protruding one.
%
% This is not a way of hiding the overfull count build.sh asserts. It changes what TeX DOES:
% the text now fits the measure and the badness is reported as an underfull box instead,
% which build.sh counts and prints and deliberately does not fail on -- a loose line is
% ugly, a protruding line is wrong, and only one of those is a layout defect.
\setlength{\emergencystretch}{3em}
\tolerance=2000

% ---- RECIPE step 16 · references ------------------------------------------------------
% natbib author-date over chicago.bst. MEASURED at wealthTensor-94: the four manuscripts
% contain ZERO \cite commands and the repository contains no .bib file -- every paper
% carries a hand-written "## References" section. natbib is loaded exactly as the recipe
% specifies, and bibtex is a NO-OP on this corpus. Recorded in LAYOUT-MANIFEST.json as a
% measurement rather than worked around.
\usepackage[authoryear,round]{natbib}

% ---- the manuscripts number themselves --------------------------------------------------
% MEASURED, from the rendered page: every heading in the corpus already carries its own
% number ("## 2 · The model", "### 2.1 · The process"), so LaTeX's counter produced
% "14  2 · The model" and "14.1  2.1 · The process" -- two numbering schemes disagreeing
% with each other on the same line, and the LaTeX one wrong because the four papers are
% concatenated. Pandoc's own generated preamble does exactly this, for exactly this reason.
\setcounter{secnumdepth}{-\maxdimen}

% ---- RECIPE step 11 · headings, on the 1.18 scale -------------------------------------
% Title 17.5/20.0 (Libertinus Serif Display); section 13.0/15.0; subsection 12.0/14.0;
% subsubsection 11.0/14.0, Libertinus Serif Bold. Vertical skips are whole and half
% multiples of the 14.0pt leading, so a heading cannot push the rest of a page off the
% grid of step 9.
\makeatletter
\renewcommand\section{\@startsection{section}{1}{\z@}%
  {-21.0pt \@plus -2.0pt \@minus -2.0pt}{7.0pt}%
  {\normalfont\fontsize{13.0}{15.0}\selectfont\bfseries\raggedright}}
\renewcommand\subsection{\@startsection{subsection}{2}{\z@}%
  {-14.0pt \@plus -2.0pt \@minus -2.0pt}{3.5pt}%
  {\normalfont\fontsize{12.0}{14.0}\selectfont\bfseries\raggedright}}
\renewcommand\subsubsection{\@startsection{subsubsection}{3}{\z@}%
  {-14.0pt \@plus -2.0pt \@minus -2.0pt}{3.5pt}%
  {\normalfont\fontsize{11.0}{14.0}\selectfont\bfseries\raggedright}}
\renewcommand\paragraph{\@startsection{paragraph}{4}{\z@}%
  {14.0pt \@plus 2.0pt \@minus 2.0pt}{-0.5em}%
  {\normalfont\fontsize{11.0}{14.0}\selectfont\bfseries}}
\makeatother

% ---- P13a · the stamp values, written by build.sh, never by hand ----------------------
% \wtdoclabel names WHICH document this is, in the footer of every page. It exists
% because a review build produced from a different manuscript set is byte-for-byte
% plausible as the canonical capture -- same fonts, same measure, same stamp shape --
% and the only thing standing between a reader and that confusion is this string.
% build.sh sets it from WT_DOCLABEL; the default is the canonical capture.
\providecommand{\wtdoclabel}{wealth-tensor capture}
% build.sh generates wt-stamp.tex containing \wtcommit and \wtbuilt. \wtbuilt is the
% COMMIT's date, not the wall clock: a build timestamp would change the footer on every
% page on every rebuild, which would change every per-page text hash, which would make
% LAYOUT-MANIFEST.json unreproducible BY CONSTRUCTION. The stamp has to be a function of
% the commit alone or it defeats the row it exists to satisfy.
\input{wt-stamp.tex}

% ---- P13a · THE COMMIT STAMP, VISIBLY ON THE PAGE -------------------------------------
% P13a asks for "a point-in-time capture that CANNOT BE CONFUSED WITH A LATER ONE". The
% commit therefore appears on the title page AND in the footer of EVERY page, so no single
% sheet of a printed copy is ambiguous about which capture it came from. \wtcommit and
% \wtbuilt are injected by build.sh from `git rev-parse HEAD`; they are never typed by hand.
%
% ps@plain is redefined as well as the new style, deliberately: \maketitle, \part and
% longtable's first page all issue \thispagestyle{plain}, and a page that escaped the stamp
% would be exactly the ambiguity this row exists to prevent.
\makeatletter
\newcommand{\wt@footline}{%
  \parbox{\textwidth}{\centering\normalfont\fontsize{8.0}{10.0}\selectfont
    \wtdoclabel\quad\textbullet\quad\texttt{\wtcommit}%
    \quad\textbullet\quad\wtbuilt\quad\textbullet\quad\thepage}}
\newcommand{\ps@wtcapture}{%
  \renewcommand{\@oddhead}{}\renewcommand{\@evenhead}{}%
  \renewcommand{\@oddfoot}{\wt@footline}\renewcommand{\@evenfoot}{\wt@footline}}
\renewcommand{\ps@plain}{\ps@wtcapture}
\makeatother
\pagestyle{wtcapture}

% ---- the paper title block (the title scale of step 11) -------------------------------
\newcommand{\wtpapertitle}[1]{%
  {\wtdisplayfont\fontsize{17.5}{20.0}\selectfont\raggedright #1\par}%
  \nopagebreak\vspace{14.0pt}}

% ---- wide tables, ONE WIDTH PER TABLE --------------------------------------------------
% A nine-column table cannot live inside a 289.08pt measure, and step 8 leaves 162.6075pt of
% margin on each side for it not to have to. But a UNIFORM wide measure is the wrong repair
% and the rendered page said so: pandoc gives a table with any long cell a set of
% p{}-columns that are FRACTIONS OF \linewidth, so widening \linewidth for every table
% stretches a narrow two-column table to the same 460pt as a nine-column one and opens a
% canyon down its middle. Wide is not the same as needing to be wide.
%
% So each table gets its OWN measure, defaulting to the body measure and widened only where
% the build proved it necessary. docs/deliverable/TABLE-WIDTHS.tsv is that record: it is
% COMMITTED, it names each table and the overfull amount that forced its width, and build.sh
% reads it rather than re-deriving it -- so the widths are a reviewable input to the build
% and not an emergent property of it. `./build.sh --retune` regenerates it.
%
% THE GLUE IS THE SUBTLE PART AND IT WAS WRONG ONCE. \hsize is widened per table, but its
% ORIGIN is still the text block's left edge -- so giving \LTleft and \LTright equal rigid
% parts centres the table about a point half the overhang to the RIGHT of where the reader's
% eye expects, and pushes a full-width table clean off the right edge of the paper. \LTleft
% must carry the WHOLE overhang as its rigid part, with the fill doing the centring:
%     \LTleft = -(tablewidth - textwidth) plus 1fill ,   \LTright = 0pt plus 1fill
% Then a body-width table lands exactly on the text block (measured: ink 161.99-450.01bp
% against a text block of 162.0-450.0bp) and a widened one is centred on the page (measured:
% 76.84-535.77bp on a 612bp sheet). Both measured with ghostscript's bbox device, because
% THE OVERFULL COUNT CANNOT SEE THIS FAILURE -- widening \hsize silences the warning whether
% or not the ink is still on the paper. That is why build.sh also asserts page bounds.
%
% Tabular matter is set at 10.0/12.0 rather than the body's 11.0/14.0. That is ordinary in
% economics typesetting, and step 13's prohibition on shrinking type is about the CODE font,
% where a reader copies identifiers out of the PDF, and does not reach here.
\makeatletter
\newlength{\wt@tablewidth}
% build.sh writes wt-tablewidths.tex from the committed TSV; absent, every table is body width
\InputIfFileExists{wt-tablewidths.tex}{}{}
% #1 = stable table id, #2 = its column count (the tuner needs it: a cell that overflows a
% p-column by x needs the TABLE widened by about x times the number of columns).
\newenvironment{wttable}[2]
  {\par\addvspace{7.0pt}\begingroup
   \ifcsname wt@tw@#1\endcsname
     \setlength{\wt@tablewidth}{\csname wt@tw@#1\endcsname}%
   \else
     \setlength{\wt@tablewidth}{\textwidth}%
   \fi
   \def\wt@tid{#1}% an environment's END part cannot see #1; save it while still in scope
   \typeout{WT-TABLE-BEGIN:#1:#2:\the\wt@tablewidth}%
   % A table that reaches the width cap and still does not fit steps its type down instead;
   % that is the last resort and TABLE-WIDTHS.tsv records which tables took it.
   \ifcsname wt@ts@#1\endcsname \csname wt@ts@#1\endcsname
   \else \fontsize{10.0}{12.0}\selectfont \fi
   \setlength{\hsize}{\wt@tablewidth}%
   \setlength{\linewidth}{\wt@tablewidth}%
   \setlength{\columnwidth}{\wt@tablewidth}%
   \LTleft=-\dimexpr\wt@tablewidth-\textwidth\relax plus 1fill\relax
   \LTright=0pt plus 1fill\relax}
  {\typeout{WT-TABLE-END:\wt@tid}\endgroup\addvspace{7.0pt}\par}
\makeatother
